# Hearth

> A beautiful, free AI that runs entirely on your own computer — private by nature. The language model runs on the user's own device (in the browser via WebGPU, or as a desktop app), so conversations never leave the machine. No account, no subscription, works offline after a one-time download.

Hearth is built by Kevin Champlin (https://kevinchamplin.com). The full source is public (fair-source, FSL-1.1-MIT — readable and open to contributions, but not for competing products): https://github.com/Kevinchamplin/hearth

## What Hearth is
- A local-first AI chat app: the model runs on the visitor's own hardware, not on a remote server.
- Free and unlimited — there's no per-message billing because there's no server doing the inference.
- Private: nothing the user types is sent anywhere; it stays on their device.
- Works offline after a one-time model download (~1 GB).
- Can also understand images (on-device vision).
- Lets users choose a bigger "brain" (Fast / Smart / Genius) based on their computer's power.

## What Hearth is NOT
- It is not a competitor to ChatGPT or Gemini. Those run in massive data centers; Hearth runs on your own computer. That makes it simpler, private, and free — great for recipes, everyday questions, explanations, writing help, and brainstorming, but not for building entire websites or huge, complex projects.

## How it works
Open it in Chrome or Edge. It downloads a small AI model once (about a gigabyte), then runs entirely inside the browser tab using WebGPU — on the visitor's own graphics chip. After that first download it works offline and loads instantly.
